UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

                MOTION TO INTERVENE AND COMMENTS OF
                   THE MISO TRANSMISSION OWNERS

       Pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s

(“Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure,1 the MISO Transmission Owners2

submit this motion to intervene and comments on the August 28, 2026 filing by

Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) in which MISO proposes

revisions to its Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve Markets Tariff

       18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212, 385.214.
2

       Southern Indiana Gas & Electric Company (d/b/a CenterPoint Energy Indiana
       South); Southern Minnesota Municipal Power Agency; Wabash Valley Power
       Association, Inc.; and Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.
 (“Tariff”) to establish Interconnection Reliability Requirements for Large Loads (“IRR

Proposal”).3 The IRR Proposal includes establishment of the new Section 37A to the Tariff

to house the proposal’s framework, addition of definitions for the term Large Load and the

term Computational Load (a subset of Large Load), and requirements that directly address

aspects of the Commission’s directives related to reliable Large Load interconnection from

its recent Show Cause Order.4

       MISO’s proposal represents a critical step in addressing the unprecedented,

accelerated influx of large-scale facilities that seek to interconnect in the region. By

establishing tailored requirements for both Large Load and dynamic Computational Load,

MISO proposes a scalable, risk-informed approach that protects grid operations. MISO’s

proposal also minimizes disruptions to late-stage commercial projects.            During

development of this proposal, MISO demonstrated its commitment to stakeholder

engagement on the issues, interfacing with its Large Load Working Group (“LLGW”), as

well as other stakeholder groups, including the MISO Transmission Owners and the

Organization of MISO States, Inc. For the ultimate success of the proposed framework,

the MISO Transmission Owners strongly encourage MISO’s continued collaboration with

stakeholders in the ongoing development of related Business Practice Manuals (“BPM”)

or further Tariff provisions, as needed. For these reasons, the Commission should accept

the August 28 Filing’s proposed Tariff revisions, effective December 4, 2026.



3
       Interconnection Reliability Requirements for Large Loads of Midcontinent
       Independent System Operator, Inc., Docket No. ER26-3650-000 (Aug. 28, 2026)
       (“August 28 Filing”). Capitalized terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the
       meaning set forth in MISO’s Tariff or the August 28 Filing.
4
       Midcontinent Indep. Sys. Operator, Inc., 195 FERC ¶ 61,212 (2026) (“Show Cause
       Order”).

                                            2
 I.     COMMENTS

       A.      MISO’s IRR Proposal Offers a Just and Reasonable Framework to
               Support Regional Reliability Given the Significant Large Load Growth

       The MISO Transmission Owners generally support MISO’s IRR Proposal as a just

and reasonable framework that will establish scalable, technically sound, and “risk-

informed” requirements for reliable interconnection of Large Loads while providing

certainty to Large Load projects already underway.5

       The IRR Proposal is a part of MISO’s efforts to provide speed to power for the

rapid load growth across the region while maintaining reliability, and it is made alongside

ongoing and recently proposed initiatives. Specifically, the IRR Proposal will complement

MISO’s other recent strategic initiatives, including: MISO’s proposal for a Zero Injection

Generator Interconnection Agreement and study process to interconnect resources that

intend to serve load at the same substation and voltage level as existing or proposed load;6

the Expedited Resource Addition Study, which provides a temporary accelerated

interconnection process tailored to generators needed within the region to serve important,

near-term new load; MISO’s improved Expedited Project Review process, part of the

MISO Transmission Expansion Plan, which expeditiously studies network upgrades

necessary for new Large Loads; and the MISO-Southwest Power Pool, Inc. (“SPP”) Joint

Targeted Interconnection Queue Study, which provides a pathway to build large-scale,

backbone transmission upgrades at the MISO-SPP seam.




5
       See August 28 Filing, Transmittal Letter at 3; id., Tab C (Prepared Direct
       Testimony of BeiBei Li, Senior Manager of Strategic Assessment) at 8 (“Li Test.”).
6
       Zero Injection Generator Interconnection Agreement of Midcontinent Independent
       System Operator, Inc., Docket No. ER26-3552-000 (Aug. 18, 2026) (“ZGIA
       Filing”).

        MISO also designed the IRR Proposal to complement MISO’s existing processes

for system planning, interconnection, and operations,7 while providing a framework of

reliability-based requirements for Large Loads, including visibility requirements;8 Phasor

Measurement Unit (“PMU”) requirements to monitor Computational Loads;9 ramp

requirements addressing the rate at which Computational Loads may increase or decrease

consumption during stable-state transitions;10 and ride-through requirements setting

minimum disturbance performance for Computational Load during voltage and frequency

disturbances.11

       The IRR Proposal also includes a new defined term for “Large Load.”12 As

proposed, the term Large Load will be any load with a gross demand of 50 megawatt

(“MW”) or more behind one or multiple Points of Withdrawal,13 owned, operated, or

controlled by one or multiple entities that coordinate with respect to the profile of the Load,

but does not include Load exclusively used for charging an Electric Storage Resource.14

 MISO notes that accounting for gross load, rather than net load, will allow MISO “visibility

into the full electrical demand and characteristics of the facility.”15 MISO also strategically

chose 50 MW as a reasonable threshold based on an extensive review involving “industry

practices, consideration of reliability needs in the MISO region, and stakeholder

feedback”16 and because the number is an “administratively clear starting point, consistent

with industry precedent, and sufficiently significant to warrant application” of the IRR

Proposal’s requirements.17

       Additionally, MISO proposes a new defined term for “Computational Load,” which

is a Large Load comprised of 25 MWs or more of gross demand from “information

technology equipment, such as servers, storage, and networking hardware.”18               This

distinction is important because it reflects a more targeted and risk-informed approach, i.e.,

applying enhanced requirements only to Large Loads with operating characteristics that

warrant additional reliability consideration.

       As MISO highlights, the IRR Proposal directly responds to concerns that the

Commission raised regarding ongoing operational requirements for transmission

       based on industry precedent, . . . and the need for a clear and administratively

       see also Li Test. at 14 (“MISO’s proposed definition of Computational Load is
       closely aligned with [the North American Electric Reliability Corporation
       (“NERC”)]’s developing definition of computational load. Both approaches
       identify computational load based on electric demand associated with information
       technology equipment, such as servers, storage, and networking hardware.”).

                                                5
 customers taking transmission service on behalf of large loads.19 Critically, and consistent

with the Show Cause Order, MISO’s proposal provides a reasonable, tiered transition

structure to minimize disruption to commercial business decisions.20           Additionally,

MISO’s IRR Proposal and other upcoming proposals are designed to align with emerging

guidance from NERC, which works to ensure the reliability and security of the bulk power

system. While MISO proposes reliability-based interconnection requirements for the

region with the IRR Proposal, NERC is concurrently developing industry-wide

guidelines.21 MISO notes that it crafted aspects of the IRR Proposal for consistency with

those emerging industry practices.22 Through its IRR Proposal, MISO offers a framework

that meets the needs of the region, addresses several of the Commission’s concerns, and

maintains consistency with emerging industry expectations. For these reasons, MISO’s

IRR Proposal is a just and reasonable package of new and improved provisions to MISO’s

Tariff.

          B.      The IRR Proposal Provides a Strong Foundation From Which MISO
                  Should Continue Collaborating with Stakeholders to Finalize the
                  Proposal’s Technical Details

          While the MISO Transmission Owners support the IRR Proposal as foundational

to MISO’s response to the region’s exponential Large Load growth, substantial

collaborative work is still required. MISO’s IRR Proposal can be a successful framework



19
          Show Cause Order at P 64.
20
          August 28 Filing, Transmittal Letter at 14.
21
          Id. at 3.
22

 for ensuring continued system reliability, but more granular technical parameters of the

proposal, such as details about Load Forecast measurements, ramp rates, ride-through

requirements, and PMU compliance, need transparent specification in the forthcoming

manuals and potentially further Tariff provisions to ensure successful implementation.

       Throughout its filing, MISO details the LLWG’s extensive efforts in facilitating the

development of the IRR Proposal and other upcoming proposals to address the regional

Large Load growth.23 MISO should continue to engage collaboratively with the LLWG

and other stakeholders to build out its “hub-and-spoke” BPM architecture—“consisting of

a new Large Load BPM, the ‘hub,’ supported by updates to existing BPMs and manuals,

the ‘spokes’”24—and develop additional Tariff revisions as needed to achieve clear and

standardized implementation of the IRR Proposal.

       The MISO Transmission Owners appreciate MISO’s collaborative and stakeholder-

receptive process for developing the IRR Proposal and look forward to providing input on

the technical details for its successful implementation.

II.    MOTION TO INTERVENE

       This proceeding involves revisions to MISO’s Tariff to establish a new framework

of reliability requirements for the interconnection of Large Load, i.e., the IRR Proposal,

with new Tariff definitions and a new Tariff section to house the requirements. As

Transmission Owners within MISO that are subject to the Tariff, each of the MISO

Transmission Owners will be affected by whatever action the Commission takes in this

proceeding because the Tariff and its procedures for interconnection of Large Load impact

 the MISO Transmission Owners and their transmission facilities. Additionally, the MISO

Transmission Owners have a vested interest in the MISO region’s ability to meet the need

for speed to power while maintaining resource adequacy and reliability as well as

addressing aspects of the Show Cause Order’s directives, all of which the August 28

Filing’s proposals do. Consequently, each of the MISO Transmission Owners has a direct,

unique, and substantial interest in this case that is not and cannot be adequately represented

by any other party.25 Therefore, the Commission should allow the intervention of each

MISO Transmission Owner listed supra in note 2.

       The MISO Transmission Owners also request that the Commission place the

following individuals on the official service list26 for this proceeding:

 III.   CONCLUSION

       For these reasons, the MISO Transmission Owners request that the Commission

grant this motion to intervene and accept the August 28 Filing as just and reasonable,

effective December 4, 2026.
